blocker: Not blocked for the formal question. On the means-to-end reading of EndRequires the crux moves to WN (a rational power is fixed toward a given being only if the giver's end requires it). Rivals: the necessary diffusion of the good (Plotinus; Avicenna's First as standardly reported), Rowe's argument, Kretzmann's Dionysian argument; Leibniz's moral necessity is not a metaphysical fixity. A rival granting the common root's direct reach, intellect, willed giving, one power, (b1) and SS must deny WN; which premise the historical Avicennian system denies is unresolved (unread): if its emanation is mediated (Ilahiyyat IX.4, navigation), it denies direct reach and is the mediated-creator variant, against which N3 does nothing. Next tests: a non-modal criterion for EndRequires; formalize selective necessary diffusion against WN; read Ilahiyyat IX.4; tag G as productive or non-productive at the root.
